clue.text: Refer to a principal and force a decision

definitions.meaning: taken literally, to pass a matter up to the boss or chief
idiom for making a situation come to a crisis that demands resolution

explanation.surface: Escalating a matter to the boss in order to get it settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means passing something to the chief, and idiomatically means bringing matters to a crisis point.

clue.text: Confirm that Teddy is not at home

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear
someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: Checking whether a man called Teddy is genuinely absent from his house.
explanation.definitionFit: To corroborate a claim is to support or verify it, a synonym of confirm.

clue.text: One mother who leads Moslems in prayer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
mam is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother who leads a congregation of Muslims in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer leader of a mosque is given this Arabic title.

clue.text: King George relaxed when given a butter spread

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
eased means loosened or relaxed

explanation.surface: A king named George unwinds once he is served buttered bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Smeared with butter or fat describes a pan or tin that has been prepared.

clue.text: Playing while travelling by coach

definitions.meaning: a stagecoach was a horse-drawn coach, so travelling by one is going on it

explanation.surface: An actor performing while touring on a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors performing are in front of the audience; old stagecoach passengers rode aboard one.

clue.text: High temperatures can be a trial

definitions.meaning: a preliminary race in a competition that decides who goes through

explanation.surface: Hot weather can be an ordeal to endure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is the physical sense; a qualifying round in athletics is the sporting sense.

clue.text: Worry only if it is set in stone

indicators.note: set in tells us one word is placed inside another, like a jewel mounted in a setting

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Only fret if the matter is fixed and unchangeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only if' and 'is' are link words; 'set in stone' looks like the idiom for permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or disturb someone is to make them anxious, a verb sense of worry.

clue.text: Say goodbye and go on holiday

definitions.meaning: taking leave from work means a holiday

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell before heading off on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means departing politely, and read literally means using time off work.

clue.text: Tories to hit at sacred TUC principle

parts.note: the Tories are the political right
taken as written
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: Conservatives attacking a cherished trade union tenet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Unions hold that workers may withdraw their labour, a core entitlement they defend.

clue.text: Speedily become a top-class dancer

parts.note: tap stands for a tap dancer
an ace is someone top-class

explanation.surface: Quickly rising to become an excellent dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is a link word: 'a top-class dancer' is A TAP ACE, the same letters as the answer differently spaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving quickly means going briskly, i.e. speedily.

clue.text: Bantu made a wish around 1.50

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are constructed into a new form
around tells us the Roman numerals are turned about

parts.note: 1 is I and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone made a wish at ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A WISH to SWAHI; 'around' turns IL into LI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most widely spoken of the Bantu family of African languages.

clue.text: Letter returned to school

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: a note is a short letter

explanation.surface: A letter sent back to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Confession of an habitual killer in the Hebrides

definitions.text: Confession of an habitual killer in the Hebrides

parts.words: Confession of an habitual killer in the Hebrides
parts.note: that phrase run together is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A serial murderer owning up somewhere in the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An island of the Inner Hebrides, noted for its whisky.

clue.text: Attempt to have a party

definitions.meaning: to have a go or try

explanation.surface: Trying to throw a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have a' is a link word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a try is a go, and a lively social gathering is a do; both are slang senses.

clue.text: A grain found in oak wood

definitions.text: A grain found in oak wood

parts.note: corn is grain

explanation.surface: A seed one comes across in a forest of oaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree is the seed lying about in oak woodland.

clue.text: New Age traveller broad in the beam

definitions.meaning: an alternative-lifestyle wanderer, often called by a sixties term

explanation.surface: A wandering alternative type who is rather wide-bottomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower-child type follows alternative ways; with wide haunches someone is big-hipped.

clue.text: Observed that champagne was at room temperature

explanation.surface: Somebody spotted that the bubbly had been served warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To see or spot something is to observe it; split, the word says the wine lacked chilling.

clue.text: I have reverted to depression: that'sobvious

indicators.note: reverted means the short form is turned back to front

parts.note: I have contracts to I've
a dent is a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Admitting a relapse into low spirits is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverted' turns IVE into EVI; 'depression' suggests low mood but is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain and apparent is clear to all, a synonym of obvious.

clue.text: Divers constantly immersed in salt

indicators.note: immersed in places one word inside another, as if dunked

parts.note: sal is Latin and chemical for salt, as in sal volatile
ever means always or constantly

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers are always submerged in brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is not people who dive but the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective for sundry or various means a number of.

clue.text: Tax one is allowed to take from Italian enclave

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
one is the Roman numeral I
can means is permitted

explanation.surface: A levy someone may deduct from an Italian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take from' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal city-state is surrounded by Rome, an independent enclave within Italy.

clue.text: Prominent people compose editorials

explanation.surface: Important figures write the newspaper's opinion pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compose' is a link word; in British newspapers editorials are called leading articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of groups are chiefs; leading articles in papers are opinion columns.

clue.text: Make dispirited editor return to his professional field

indicators.note: return means the abbreviation goes back to front

parts.note: an editor works in journalism, known as the press

explanation.surface: Get an editor down by sending him back to journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ED into DE; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to sadden or deject them.

clue.text: Makes up one's mind twelve days before Christmas

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
the Ides of December fall on the 13th, twelve days before the 25th

explanation.surface: Settling a matter twelve days ahead of the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Roman calendar the Ides of December is the 13th.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or resolve something is to reach a conclusion.

clue.text: Title is changed for a non-egalitarian

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A title gets altered for a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes in rule by a select few opposes equality.

clue.text: Consumes a portion of meat stew

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eats a helping of meat casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to take it in, which is what consumes means here.

clue.text: Put a blight on church parade

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blight

explanation.surface: Spoiling a church procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession of marchers is a demonstration walk, as is a parade.

clue.text: They bore him barefac'd on the "(Hamlet)

definitions.text: They bore him barefac'd on the "(Hamlet)

parts.words: They bore him barefac'd on the "(Hamlet)
parts.note: fill the gap in Ophelia's mad song from Hamlet: the missing word is the stand on which a corpse is carried

explanation.surface: A quotation from Ophelia's song in Shakespeare's Hamlet with its last word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable stand on which a coffin or corpse is carried to the grave.

clue.text: An alcoholic can gain nothing

parts.note: to win is to gain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A drunkard might profit not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word, though it hints at a can of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-and-out heavy drinker is slang for a habitual drunkard.

clue.text: Small number backing Anglicans in the past

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: no is short for number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A minority supported members of the Church of England formerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at one time, is a synonym of in the past.

clue.text: Climber invests a couple of hundred for medical protection

indicators.note: invests means wraps round or encloses, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two are CC

explanation.surface: A mountaineer puts money into a couple of hundred units for health cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An injection that confers immunity against a disease protects the body.

clue.text: Demand payment from Scottish church for French port

parts.note: to dun is to press for payment of a debt
kirk is the Scots word for church

explanation.surface: Asking a Scottish church to settle up for a French harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town on the north coast of France, famous for the 1940 evacuation.

clue.text: Non-scientist by disposition self-contradictory

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone without scientific training tends by nature to contradict themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by disposition' reads as 'by temperament' but signals rearranging NONSCIENTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking consistency, a statement that conflicts with itself is self-contradictory.
